title: Forklift operating condition and maintenance practice questions
description: Free forklift practice questions on 29 CFR 1910.178(p) and (q): unsafe trucks, fueling, repairs, parts, examination, mufflers and cleaning.

questions.question: A powered industrial truck was taken out of service under 1910.178(p)(1) because it was found to be unsafe. What ends that out-of-service period?

options.A: One full shift has passed
options.B: The truck has been restored to safe operating condition
options.C: The operator has signed a written waiver
options.D: A supervisor has noted the problem in a log

questions.explanation: "If at any time a powered industrial truck is found to be in need of repair, defective, or in any way unsafe, the truck shall be taken out of service until it has been restored to safe operating condition."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A truck's exhaust system emits hazardous sparks. Under 1910.178(q)(8), when may the truck be returned to service?

options.A: After the engine has cooled for 30 minutes
options.B: At the next daily examination, whatever its result
options.C: Right away, if it is used only outdoors
options.D: When the cause for the emission of such sparks and flames has been eliminated

questions.explanation: A vehicle that emits hazardous sparks or flames from the exhaust system "shall immediately be removed from service, and not returned to service until the cause for the emission of such sparks and flames has been eliminated."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which condition does 1910.178(q)(9) name as the reason to remove a vehicle from service for overheating?

options.A: The temperature of a part is found to be in excess of its normal operating temperature, thus creating a hazardous condition
options.B: The outside air temperature rises above 90 °F
options.C: The engine has run for more than one full shift
options.D: The operator's cab feels warm to the touch

questions.explanation: "When the temperature of any part of any truck is found to be in excess of its normal operating temperature, thus creating a hazardous condition, the vehicle shall be removed from service" until the cause for such overheating has been eliminated.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Fueling, fuel leaks and open flames
questions.question: With the engine shut off, a refueling attendant routinely fills truck fuel tanks until they overflow onto the floor. Under 1910.178(p)(2), what is wrong with this practice?

options.A: Nothing; (p)(2) covers only filling while the engine is running
options.B: Nothing, as long as the floor is mopped by the end of the shift
options.C: Spillage shall be avoided, and letting the tank overflow does not avoid it
options.D: Fuel tanks may be filled only by a supervisor

questions.explanation: 1910.178(p)(2) reads: "Fuel tanks shall not be filled while the engine is running. Spillage shall be avoided." The second sentence applies even when the engine is off.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Fueling, fuel leaks and open flames
questions.question: A truck has a leak in its fuel system. Under 1910.178(p)(4), what must happen before it is operated?

options.A: The fuel tank has been emptied
options.B: The leak has been reported to a supervisor
options.C: The leak has been corrected
options.D: The truck has been moved outdoors

questions.explanation: "No truck shall be operated with a leak in the fuel system until the leak has been corrected."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Fueling, fuel leaks and open flames
questions.question: Under 1910.178(p)(5), what shall not be used for checking the electrolyte level in storage batteries or the gasoline level in fuel tanks?

options.A: Open flames
options.B: A dipstick
options.C: A sight gauge
options.D: The truck's fuel gauge

questions.explanation: "Open flames shall not be used for checking electrolyte level in storage batteries or gasoline level in fuel tanks."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which two requirements does 1910.178(q)(1) set for a power-operated industrial truck that is not in safe operating condition?

options.A: It shall be tagged, and it may be used until a repair is scheduled
options.B: It shall be removed from service, and its usual operator shall repair it
options.C: It shall be reported to OSHA, and anyone on the shift may repair it
options.D: It shall be removed from service, and all repairs shall be made by authorized personnel

questions.explanation: "Any power-operated industrial truck not in safe operating condition shall be removed from service. All repairs shall be made by authorized personnel."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: In which locations does 1910.178(q)(2) say no repairs shall be made?

options.A: Any building with a sprinkler system
options.B: Class I, II, and III locations
options.C: Any area within 10 feet of a loading dock
options.D: Any location on the ground floor

questions.explanation: The rule states: "No repairs shall be made in Class I, II, and III locations."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A truck needs repairs to its fuel and ignition systems that involve fire hazards. Where does 1910.178(q)(3) say those repairs shall be conducted?

options.A: Only in locations designated for such repairs
options.B: Anywhere, as long as a fire extinguisher is nearby
options.C: Only outdoors at night
options.D: At the spot where the truck broke down

questions.explanation: "Those repairs to the fuel and ignition systems of industrial trucks which involve fire hazards shall be conducted only in locations designated for such repairs."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A part of an industrial truck needs replacement. What does 1910.178(q)(5) require of the replacement part?

options.A: It shall be the lowest-cost part available
options.B: It shall be approved by the OSHA area office
options.C: It shall be a used part taken from another truck of any make
options.D: It shall be equivalent as to safety with those used in the original design

questions.explanation: "All parts of any such industrial truck requiring replacement shall be replaced only by parts equivalent as to safety with those used in the original design."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: To save weight, a maintenance shop proposes removing a part the manufacturer installed on a fork truck. The change is not part of a conversion under paragraph (q)(12). What does 1910.178(q)(6) say?

options.A: It may be done if the operator agrees
options.B: It may be done for parts that weigh under 10 pounds
options.C: Trucks shall not be altered by the elimination of any parts
options.D: It may be done if the truck is used only outdoors

questions.explanation: Industrial trucks shall not be altered "either by the addition of extra parts not provided by the manufacturer or by the elimination of any parts, except as provided in paragraph (q)(12) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.178(q)(6), the relative positions of a truck's various parts shall not be altered from what?

options.A: What they were at the last daily examination
options.B: What they were when originally received from the manufacturer
options.C: What the operator finds most comfortable
options.D: What they were after the most recent repair

questions.explanation: "Industrial trucks shall not be altered so that the relative positions of the various parts are different from what they were when originally received from the manufacturer".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Paragraph (q)(6) makes an exception for paragraph (q)(12). What change to a truck does (q)(12) allow?

options.A: Converting any truck to diesel fuel without approval
options.B: Converting a truck originally approved for gasoline to liquefied petroleum gas fuel, provided the complete conversion results in a truck which embodies the features specified for LP or LPS designated trucks
options.C: Removing the overhead guard on trucks used indoors
options.D: Adding counterweight without the manufacturer's approval

questions.explanation: Trucks "originally approved for the use of gasoline for fuel may be converted to liquefied petroleum gas fuel provided the complete conversion results in a truck which embodies the features specified for LP or LPS designated trucks."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A shop converts a truck originally approved for gasoline to liquefied petroleum gas fuel, using a conversion kit it built itself that has not been approved. Does this meet 1910.178(q)(12)?

options.A: Yes, because (q)(12) allows any gasoline truck to be converted to LP gas
options.B: Yes, if the shop has done similar conversions before
options.C: Yes, if the operator has been trained on LP-gas trucks
options.D: No, because such conversion equipment shall be approved

questions.explanation: 1910.178(q)(12) allows the conversion and then says "Such conversion equipment shall be approved." A kit that has not been approved does not meet that requirement.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which industrial trucks does 1910.178(q)(7) say shall be examined after each shift?

options.A: Trucks used on a round-the-clock basis
options.B: Trucks that run on liquefied petroleum gas
options.C: Trucks used outdoors
options.D: Trucks more than ten years old

questions.explanation: "Where industrial trucks are used on a round-the-clock basis, they shall be examined after each shift."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1910.178(q)(7) require when defects are found?

options.A: They shall be noted and fixed at the next scheduled service
options.B: They shall be reported only if the truck has stopped working
options.C: They shall be immediately reported and corrected
options.D: They shall be listed in a monthly summary

questions.explanation: "Defects when found shall be immediately reported and corrected."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.178(q)(8), water mufflers shall be filled daily or as frequently as is necessary to prevent the supply of water from dropping below what level?

options.A: 25 percent of the filled capacity
options.B: 50 percent of the filled capacity
options.C: 10 percent of the filled capacity
options.D: 75 percent of the filled capacity

questions.explanation: "Water mufflers shall be filled daily or as frequently as is necessary to prevent depletion of the supply of water below 75 percent of the filled capacity."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A vehicle's muffler has screens that may become clogged, and they are clogged now. What does 1910.178(q)(8) say?

options.A: The vehicle shall not be operated while such screens or parts are clogged
options.B: The vehicle may be operated if the windows are open
options.C: The vehicle may be operated until the end of the week
options.D: The vehicle may be operated at idle speed only

questions.explanation: "Vehicles with mufflers having screens or other parts that may become clogged shall not be operated while such screens or parts are clogged."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.178(q)(10), industrial trucks shall be kept in a clean condition, free of which materials?

options.A: Dust, paint chips, and labels
options.B: Lint, excess oil, and grease
options.C: Rust, water spots, and mud
options.D: Tape, chalk marks, and stickers

questions.explanation: "Industrial trucks shall be kept in a clean condition, free of lint, excess oil, and grease."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A plant switches to a new high flash point cleaning solvent that is more toxic than the one it used before. Under 1910.178(q)(10), what must the precautions regarding toxicity, ventilation, and fire hazard match?

options.A: The size of the truck
options.B: The precautions used for the old solvent
options.C: The agent or solvent used
options.D: The time of day the cleaning is done

questions.explanation: 1910.178(q)(10) says "High flash point (at or above 100 °F.) solvents may be used. Precautions regarding toxicity, ventilation, and fire hazard shall be consonant with the agent or solvent used."
